items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: So this thing was in unison that we were playing.

ctx.x: comes walking in around 11:30. By now, Tommy's fuse is lit. He's so mad he cannot be contained, you know, and one word led to another and we started in, you know. And we played it, it was a thing in unison, and we finished the thing. Little rings, we were doing. And Benny just kept on playing, like that, so Tommy said, "All right, Benny. We all know how good you play. Now come on, let's do this and get out of here. We've been here all morning." And one word led to another. Tommy threw his trombone at me and I…

Another thing that happened there, Louis Armstrong, you know, always played a little bit sharp. I mean all musicians know that. So this thing was in unison that we were playing. So Emil Newman, who was the musical director for this thing, he said, "Look, you get Pops aside and talk to him." So I got Pops over and I'm talking to him, and I see Emil go over and he gets the trumpet and he pulls the slide out about an inch, or an inch and a half or something. Now, he comes over and he says, "Okay." So we come back and
we start the thing again, and Louis's just as sharp as he was before. In other words, that's the way he heard it, and moving the slide didn't mean a thing.
